spans.text: A week after the Paldiski Submarine Base incident.
■FILE■ NUSSRA920640605190087, decrypting...
Sir, Griffin is still putting up a fight.
Don't forget our objective... That base is the most important thing here.
Someone pauses the playback, and the Nyto who was originally seated and taking notes in the camera room rises nervously to her feet.
This is a routine weekly briefing, but the crushing atmosphere drills a message into the minds of all the Nytos present—slip-ups are not allowed.
Just then, a kindly female voice addresses them.
...Not this one, Susanna.
The kinder the voice, the more nervous it makes her feel.
Susanna can almost feel her palms beginning to sweat... She forces herself to calm down.
...My apologies. A moment, please.
She immediately pulls up a new file.
■FILE■ DDRA585246472307521, decrypting...
Let's say our goodbyes here.
Not going to bring back a souvenir?
Everything goes with you—that's the order I received. Remember to hand the children over to Herr Havier's safekeeping.
Now then, as unpleasant as it is, I'd better go get Ange.
My mission is to monitor her to begin with, so it'll be bad if my objective goes missing.
Understood... All the best, then.
No need to worry. We'll meet again very soon.
The voices suddenly stop again. Someone has obviously paused it once more.
This time, the woman's voice is even gentler than before.
Please—rewind it a little further back, if you don't mind.
She's even being extra polite; Susanna can no longer control her trembling.
And she knows her answer will only make the woman before her even angrier.
...I am very sorry, Big Sister Nemhran.
The influx of seawater made it impossible to recover any information from that base...
This time, Nemhran makes no reply. However, Susanna doesn't dare raise her head...
She can't let things stand as they are!
Susanna hurriedly searches through the data in her VCI.
She swiftly sifts through two people's worth of files.
Hopefully she'll find something to make up for this!
■FILE■ UO83520530300147, decrypting...
Error!!!
■FILE■ UO34678231305238, decrypting...
Error!!!
Connecting to the "Bee Sting" System...
System error, unable to connect.
Restart?
As the encrypted layer displays an error message, the Nytos return to the real camera room.
A transmission notification rings, and Susanna reflexively puts it through.
...It was just a system malfunction, don't worry.
The gentle voice flows into Susanna's ear like Satan's sweet whispers.
I... I am terribly sorry, I will organize Angelia's files and the information pertaining to the undersea base and hand them to you.
Thank you for your hard work.
Just... Just doing my job.
Retrieve Angelia's file and the info on Task Force DEFY. Convert them to plaintext, polish up the language, and then send it out.
Shall I send it to the "Chief" or to Aver—
Olga.
As Nemhran quietly speaks that name, another Nyto in the room silently steps out of the shadows.
Without any further explanation, she steps forward swiftly and breaks Susanna's neck with practiced ease.
Susanna's voice is cut off in a simple yet brutal way.
Her vocalization systems are physically destroyed with no prior warning.
Throughout the entire process, Susanna does not put up the slightest bit of resistance.
Or perhaps, she is fully aware that resistance is futile.
Do not... mention that place.
Susanna collapses to the ground... and becomes a corpse.
The Nyto called "Olga" respectfully takes over the communicator carried by the dead Nyto.
...And what is your name?
My name is Olga, Big Sister Nemhran.
I meant nothing by it. It is a Russian name.
From now on, I am called Olga, Big Sister Nemhran.
Nemhran chuckles. She seems to like how this Nyto knows the score.
Contact "Polar Bear''. We'll need to send Ange to Berlin.
Understood.
Nemhran hangs up.
There were four Nytos in the room before, but now there are only three.
After hesitating for a long time, one of the Nytos that is still standing turns to Olga.
...Susanna was always the one to contact "Polar Bear" before this. Where can we find the things she was responsible for?
Extract her memory module.
...Making a Susanna is quite demanding, aren't we going to send her back to...
She shudders, and then swallows the words she was about to say.
Send her back?
...You can forget about going back before the mission is over.
Given our worth, it's riskier to be sent back than to be buried here.
...But what about our access? Susanna had higher access than all of us.
Only Big Sister Nemhran can change the access and rules of the Bee Sting System. Should we send her a message?
Never, ever ask anything of her.
Once we complete the appropriate tasks, we will have the appropriate access.
Don't make wild guesses about things that weren't mentioned.
But...
You'd better believe me.
The room is silent once again.
Olga clears away Susanna's body with great efficiency, and the camera room looks like new again.
There is no sign that Susanna ever existed.
Inside a certain bar in St. Petersburg, Neo-Soviet Union.
A stinking drunk man is sprawled over the corner of the bar. For people who have vodka flowing in their veins, such a thing is an everyday occurrence.
He bangs on the broken service bell.
Every now and then he pokes the buttons that do nothing besides turn the lights on and off. Compared to the other drunks, this is actually quite polite.
Soon, a bartender holding a blended drink pats him on the shoulder.
Sir, someone ordered a German Mary for you.
The man opens his bloodshot eyes and snorts.
Izzit a Berlin Mary or a Bremen Mary?
...This drink was made with wine imported from Bremen.
Those words seem to activate the neurons within the man's brain, and his flushed cheeks tremble as he curses loudly enough that even the noisy music within the bar cannot cover it up.
I only drink Berlin Mary! What the hell are you serving me? This place is garbage!
He is clearly angry, and swats the tray that the bartender is holding to the ground.
Berlin Mary is the only true Mary!
The bartender struggles to keep his cool, but in the end all he can do is maintain his bartender's smile.
Sir, we have always served wine imported from Bremen. Perhaps you might have drunk German Marys in other places.
Would you like to try our new seasonal products? This is the latest brand. Many of our customers have ordered it.
The drunk man pushes the bartender aside and stumbles out the door.
The bartender doesn't say anything. Instead, he bends down to clean up the broken glass.
The bar resumes its usual clamor, and a lady approaches the bartender who is cleaning up in silence. She speaks into his ear.
I've already covered his tab. Good luck tonight.
An hour later, there is quite an upheaval at Paradeus' Moscow base.
...Oh no, we didn't send Ange to Berlin as planned... She's gone to Bremen!
Prepare an encrypted transmission right now.
Are we going to ask her for help? Didn't you say we shouldn't ask Big Sister Nemhran any questions?
What kind of accident was this, why did the plane end up going to Bremen...
Did Polar Bear get the location wrong? What an amateurish mistake...
...Accidents aren't the scariest.
Failure is.
But a mistake of this level won't be forgiven!
...Quiet down!
Things like this happen all the time.
Very often, what some call an accident is actually an opportunity.
We won't be implicated because of something like this.
Then why did Susanna die just because she missed out a bit of information? She made fewer mistakes than we did!
I don't think it's because she revealed... that place.
That's where you're wrong.
She affected Father's plan.
Any of our sisters who affects Father's plan is a sinner.
...Have you heard that rumor?
What rumor?
Big Sister Nemhran was cast out... She no longer enjoys Father's affection.
That's why she can't fail, and that's why she expects us not to fail either.
If I were you, I'd keep my ears and mouth shut.
That way I wouldn't make such basic mistakes.
What do you mean?
Do you know what the name of the Bee Sting System means?
—It gets in everywhere.
Not just against enemies, but us too.
That was the last thing she heard.
An all-pervasive surveillance system would naturally include the Nytos themselves.
Within the multiple-encrypted layer, Olga regularly checks the clarity of the signal.
She is responsible for taking notes during this three-person meeting, but she has no right to speak.
After a long silence, one of them finally breaks the silence.
You're the one asking me for help, Big Sister Nemhran.
I hope you'll understand Father's arrangements. I'm simply allocating assignments, No. 10954.
There is no longer a No. 10954. There is only Morridow.
Oh yes, you'd better come up with a suitable excuse for Father concerning the escape of No. 10876.
...If I'm not mistaken, she escaped on YOUR watch.
Do you have any proof of that?
Big Sister Nemhran, your Bee Sting System ought to be retired.
Destroying that information took less than ten hours.
Perhaps you call the shots in Moscow, but Berlin and Bremen are my territory.
Even if the destination hadn't changed, you wouldn't be able to interfere.
Going by the data, she is far more perfect than you.
Let's make this simple—I want to make a deal.
Let's hear it.
The mission ought to have been finished on time. That was what Father had hoped.
The reason why you're sitting here is because you want to bargain, so if you can compromise a little, I believe your requests will be more easily fulfilled.
Don't you already know what I want?
I want her location in exchange for the mission concerning Ange.
And the Boxes of Iaso.
Is she really worth it?
You should be asking yourself that.
I'm sure dear sister Machlian would be very happy to know where she stands in my heart.
Congratulations, you've come out ahead in this exchange.
Now then, as my senior, what wise words will you leave me with before this meeting ends?
As long as you're using that face, don't say things that it wouldn't speak.
Relax. I'm allowing a part of my true self to show because I trust you.
Besides, aren't keeping secrets and leaking them your forte?
I had to prepare for a full week just to contact you.
Would someone as "trusted" by Father as yourself ever disappoint me?
As that syrupy-sweet chuckle fades, Morridow's signal vanishes from the encrypted layer.
Olga finishes her data logs and carefully glances at Nemhran's expression before she finishes archiving them.
■FILE■ ROTT46532528123234... I'm sending these three files and their relevant documentation to you.
There's also a backup copy in the base layer.
I've already made two copies of the log from just now and attached Big Sister Morridow's portion to her file.
No need for that. Keep everything you see as it is—intact.
No matter which conversation it is or whether I'm around.
You are to record every single word I say.
...My apologies, I was trying to be clever.
If she had realized that, like you, then this wouldn't have come up.
Nobody cares about 10876's disappearance other than her.
...Yes, 10876 was close, but you're the most perfect.
I'm clearly not the most perfect one.
Nobody is.
Meanwhile, at the Gray Institute of Biotechnology, the woman lying within the recovery capsule opens her eyes.
Gray, who is standing to the side, opens the transparent cover.
Teacher.
As I expected, that woman agreed.
Now all the missions that Father regards as most important are within our grasp.
Gray, this is an excellent opportunity, both for me and you.
All the preparation work is complete.
You are the one I trust most, so I will hand the means of contacting her to you and nobody else.
If anything happens, you must take over our work here.
I hope I will never need to contact her.
Contacting her is a double-edged sword. It is something that must only be done as a last resort.
Hardly anyone dares to discuss her, and nobody understands her.
To think she holds a place of such honor in Father's heart...
That's not true. Father despises her.
I am certain of that—she was exiled to Moscow, like the rumors said.
Part of it was because of a mission, but it was also because Father himself wished for it.
Still, she possesses something we all rely on—the Bee Sting System.
That is the most unusual thing about her.
Each of our sisters has their own personality, and naturally they have their own strengths and weaknesses.
But she is very difficult to read. She has emotions, but no... desires.
Do you mean—she is not so much a Nyto as a tool?
...That is a very apt description.
But that is also why she will never win Father's approval.
We need hearts filled with wisdom, courage, loyalty and sacrifice.
The only thing that is unnecessary is rationality.
So she is abnormal.
Let me rephrase that—she is the only abnormality who is PERMITTED to exist.
...I understand.
Cheer up, I'm going to Bremen to receive our gift.
A week after falling into the River Weser.
This is the week in review with DFF—
The Junkers transport craft JU-094 from Bremen city veered off course and crashed into the River Weser a week ago. No civilians were hurt...
We're awaiting for the authorities to provide us with further information.
■FILE■ PACC76589264100147, decrypting...
■FILE■ PACC35426159108760, decrypting...
A scene resolves into clarity on the screen—against a chaotic backdrop, a woman is shoved into a certain bar.
Not a single person in this bar is a genuine customer.
They are either from the Stasi, PMCs, or some other factions.
We are not enemies, Angelia.
On the contrary... We are the closest comrades-in-arms.
You and me? Ha... I doubt that.
Someone whose hands are even bloodier than mine is preaching to me about "all things bright and beautiful"? Bah.
We share a common goal, Ange.
I know you can't argue with that... Our methods may be different.
But our aspiration is the same—everything we do is for the sake of Rossartrism.
"Common destiny"... I've grown tired of this kind of rhetoric.
You may be able to fool the sheep in your country with that, but don't bother using it on me.
Have you never wondered why Zelinsky and Mikhail let you come to Germany?
The data is correct. No errors detected.
Olga continues the encryption with practiced skill.
The person on the other end of the line seems to have been waiting for a long time and she is starting to get annoyed.
I might be patient, but even patience has its limits.
I apologize. We are organizing the data you requested.
I hold you in great respect. However, there are strict protocols of confidentiality for information on our end and decrypting them will require some time. I apologize for making you wait so long.
I am not here to make excuses on Teacher's behalf for our previous mistakes, but for the sake of the mission.
We may have suffered a slight setback concerning the Angelia mission, but it is not a failure.
However, I have lost contact with Teacher, so I believe Big Sister Nemhran ought to see me.
You, on the other hand, do not deserve to engage in conversation with me.
Big Sister Gray, I apologize for not being able to live up to your expectations given my status.
However, what I wish to say is—everything said by everyone who uses the Bee Sting System will be logged, and the things you have instructed me to do will reach Big Sister Nemhran's ears.
Contacting Father is an easy thing for us.
Big Sister Gray... While I do not presume to offer you any suggestions...
If you had planned to do something like that, you would not be wasting your time here waiting.
You had better hope you don't regret that.
The ripples from the top are working their way downwards, and things are spiraling out of control.
Big Sister Nemhran, we need help.
Olga doesn't say anything. All that can be heard is the sound of emotionless, mechanical whirring.
This is not a question she can answer. She has no right to do so.
Gray continues speaking.
The "Fireworks" have not yet bloomed, but we are almost out of cards.
If we reveal something that should not be revealed before then, such an outcome will be too much for any of us to atone for.
We have captured Ange, and transport of the Boxes of Iaso are proceeding according to schedule.
However, the cooperation we were promised has turned out to be very problematic, and variables have emerged in the positions of certain individuals.
I do not have the authority to make such decisions.
That is all I wish to say.
Upon finishing, the transmission immediately terminates.
This is Gray's way of expressing her grave displeasure with the situation.
Gray emerges from the recovery capsule, looking incredibly grim.
Beside her, Grig can't help but rub her shoulders.
Would you like a coffee?
We may need to start thinking about how to clean up behind us.
Why? We have not failed yet.
We need to bring our upcoming plans forward, and we had better rescue Teacher before that.
...I don't understand.
Do you think I'm being very naive?
It must look like I do not live for Father, but Teacher.
You have your reasons, but right now, you could clearly have taken her place.
No, Grig. I could never replace her.
By statistical data alone, you, me, Bramedb, and even Narciss are superior to her.
But she is the general-in-command of our activities in Berlin.
She only knows how to employ boring methods.
Your view of things is too one-sided. We are the Isomers with the highest ratings in our respective batches, but Teacher was not.
She eliminated the most perfect one in her batch.
..."Machlian"?
Do you think a Nyto who could act beneath the watchful eye of Father would be incapable?
That simply proves Father doted on her.
No, it proves that she had the ability to make Father tolerate her.
Meanwhile, our mission has already failed, because our objective is Nimogen.
If she is not here now, then what awaits us when we go back will not be pleasant.
We cannot deal with this matter, but perhaps she can.
...While I am reluctant to do so, I will accept your decision.
...I'm sorry, I didn't mean to disappoint you.
As long as I live, I will ensure you live too.
Within the encrypted layer, Olga sorts out the data that Gray gave her and hands it over to the person on the other end of the transmission.
Nemhran furrows her brow and casually scrolls through it.
I hope SOME people understood my intentions.
...Yes, Big Sister Nemhran.
I have conveyed them precisely and without error to Big Sister Gray.
A presumptuous agent will relay the wrong information to that Soviet.
Eventually, they will proceed toward the prison... assuming the Soviets are not that stupid.

I need this newcomer to be just stupid enough, but not a total moron... Humans have always had such blind faith in conclusions that they reach by themselves, as opposed to answers presented to them by others...
If the real production line is revealed, then none of you need to bother to come back.
Understood...
Also, we have already finished sending Pandora and Nimogen's data back.
Pandora's base layer is very heavily encrypted and we still have no way of cracking it... I do not understand why we kept her.
Father knows her true intentions very well... but that is also in accordance with Father's wishes.
Now is the chance to communicate with "that side", and Pandora—or the people behind her—have shown sufficient "sincerity".
Her backers have paid an adequate price to speak with Father.
Yes... I understand.
You've done enough.
You may return after this.
Yes.
Nemhran pauses, then her tone suddenly becomes much more casual.
Olga, do you think Morridow will come back?
...I'm sorry, Big Sister Nemhran.
But I cannot fathom Big Sister Morridow's thoughts.
...Her mission was definitely a failure, but I do not know how you and... how Father perceive it.
I like smart people, but I don't dislike fools.
However, fools who pretend to be smart disgust me.
Which of these do you think Morridow is, Olga?
I'm sorry, Big Sister Nemhran.
...Go ahead, speak your mind. Don't be scared.
...I dare not comment on my elder sisters' intelligence, but I can be certain that Big Sister Nemhran is one of a kind.
Elder sisters Morridow and Bramedb devote their efforts to gaining Father's attention.
Meanwhile, you are Father's capable helper.
Humans can easily replace pets, but there is no substitute for one's arms.
...His arms... Now that's an interesting metaphor.
However, you're wrong, Olga.
When humans lose their arms, they can replace them with prosthetic limbs. Such things no longer restrict them.
Click.
The transmission ends.
